title: Medical AI tested against ChatGPT; general AI outperformed #MedicalAI #HealthcareTech #AIcomparison
description: A recent study compared specialized, expensive medical AI tools with general-purpose AI models like ChatGPT on real clinical questions submitted by doctors. Despite being designed specifically for healthcare and backed by significant funding—such as Open Evidence, which recently raised $210 million—these specialized systems were outperformed by general AI models across 100 real medical queries. The evaluation was conducted by NYU researchers who had 12 doctors blindly grade answers from various AIs, including Open Evidence, UpToDate, GPT, Claude, and Gemini. Surprisingly, generalist AI models received higher rankings than dedicated medical AIs. This outcome highlights an important insight: specialized medical AIs often employ retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods, which can introduce inaccuracies when pulling information, whereas frontier language models embed extensive medical knowledge into their training, resulting in more reliable responses. The findings raise critical questions about the current adoption of medical AI in clinical settings and challenge the assumption that high cost and specialization inherently lead to better performance in healthcare decisions. This underscores the need for thorough, independent validation before deploying AI tools in sensitive environments such as hospitals. #MedicalAI #HealthcareTech #ArtificialIntelligence #OpenEvidence #ChatGPT #UpToDate #MedicalResearch #AIEvaluation #HealthcareInnovation #ClinicalDecisionSupport #RAG #GPT #Claude #GeminiAI #HospitalTechnology
